claims.quote: The new entry I found tucked behind the others was dated March 25, 1972 and said, in Hannah's small, tight hand: "March 25, 1972: A leaving asks a taking; the seam will not be satisfied without an offered place." I read it exactly as written: "A leaving asks a taking; the seam will not be satisfied without an offered place."
claims.value: "March 25, 1972: A leaving asks a taking; the seam will not be satisfied without an offered place."

claims.quote: The seam caught the light and the glass answered the way the diary promised — not with whim but with geometry. The shimmer concentrated like a held breath along the hairline; the reflected stair folded wrong again, and the blue cold in the mirror sharpened to an edge. For a second my hand and its reflection were two different clocks: mine a fraction ahead, hers a fraction late. Then the seam was a midplane and the world tightened around it.
claims.value: Under the precise alignment (lamp six feet from mantel, flame 18 in above hearth, flame aligned 7 in left of mirror centre; attic slat providing beam), the seam acts as a reflective midplane producing intensified shimmer and mirrored geometry that separates reflected and reflecting phases.

claims.quote: There was a flutter, a tilt in the lungs, and then I was looking at the parlor from the wrong side of everything: from behind the glass where the light was colder and the stair went the other way. My hands were pale, pressed to the inside of the mirror; they were me and not-me, reaching out across a surface that would not yield.

My reflection — my face, my hands — stopped matching mine and began to obey the other side. Where I lifted my hand she did not lift hers in time; instead she loosened her fingers and let them fall to her side, the small domestic motion of someone who was not astonished.
claims.value: Lena observed that her reflection ceased to synchronise and instead behaved as an independent agent corresponding to the other side's occupant.

claims.quote: On the room-side my body — my hands, my coat, my face — moved without the insistence of my will. Mrs. Haverford, who had come up the path and was in the doorway with her knitting basket, gave a small, sensible sound — a gasp... The woman in my body smiled, buttoned the cuff of my coat... and said, in my voice but not mine in intent, "Thank you, dear. I can walk now."
claims.value: ghost-hannah occupied Lena's physical body and could control it to move and speak in the house.

claims.quote: Then the seam was a midplane and the world tightened around it.
claims.value: When the beam produced symmetric incidence at the seam the conduit performed a swap: the reflected subject's state exchanged with the reflecting subject's position, effecting an identity transfer consistent with world rule 6.

claims.quote: The seam had wanted symmetry, a place offered to receive what it would let go. It asked for a taking and the house, obeying its angles, provided one.
claims.value: The diary's March 25 line indicates the ritual requires an offered 'place' and that freeing someone via the seam requires a substitution of occupants; this is a binding interpretive fact established by Lena's reading and the ritual outcome.
